svg.aria-label: feynman-technique — WITHOUT feynman-technique: I've traced it. The GET to /api/orders from http://localhost:3000 is rejected by the browser's same-origin policy before your handler runs. Because the request sets a custom header, the browser sends a preflight OPTIONS first. api.example.com returns 204 without an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so the CORS check fails and the fetch rejects with a TypeError. This is enforced client-side only, which is why the same call succeeds in curl and Postman. Your fetch and your error handling are fine. Standard remediation is to enable the cors middleware on the API and whitelist the calling origin. Apply this patch to server.js? — WITH feynman-technique: Your code didn't fail. The browser stopped it. It sent your request, got the answer back from the API, and then refused to hand it to your page. It does that because you might be signed in over there. Without the rule, any tab you have open could quietly read what sits behind your login. The API has to say your address is welcome. It never did, so the browser threw the answer away. That's also why it works in Postman and dies here. Postman has nobody to protect. Your browser has you. I can make the API say your address is welcome. Want me to add you to its list?
